name: Isolated Epispadias

criteria.description: Presence of a dorsal urethral meatus located on the dorsum of the penis or clitoris
No evidence of bladder exstrophy or other bladder anomalies
Congenital defect of the urethral plate with incomplete urethral closure
Variable degrees of urinary incontinence or dribbling

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of dorsal urethral meatus with urethral plate defect and absence of bladder exstrophy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and confirmed by physical examination; imaging may be used to exclude bladder exstrophy.

common.symptomName: Abnormality of pelvic girdle bone morphology

laboratory: Urinalysis may show signs of infection
Urine culture positive in recurrent urinary tract infections
imaging: Ultrasound to exclude bladder exstrophy and assess upper urinary tract
Voiding cystourethrogram to evaluate bladder neck and urethral anatomy
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Physical examination revealing dorsal urethral meatus and incomplete urethral closure

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of bladder exstrophy with exposed bladder mucosa
Ventral urethral opening rather than dorsal

redFlags: Signs of bladder exstrophy or abdominal wall defect
Severe urinary incontinence unresponsive to conservative management
Recurrent urinary tract infections with renal impairment
references: Gearhart JP. Epispadias and bladder exstrophy. In: Wein AJ, et al., editors. Campbell-Walsh Urology. 12th ed. Elsevier; 2020.
Baskin LS. Hypospadias and Epispadias. In: Pediatric Urology. 2018.
